themes_detail.label: Encampment Crisis Accelerating
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints spiked to 14 this week—a 600% jump from the 2.0 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 8.0)—signaling a rapid emergence of homeless encampments across Bay Ridge/Dyker Heights this week, aligning with repeated DHS funding requests in community board budget submissions.
evidence: 14 encampment complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.0 weekly baseline (600% spike, z-score 8.0)
Community board has submitted repeated 'Other request for services for the homeless' budget requests across multiple years, indicating chronic unmet need
Statistically significant anomaly meets threshold for immediate investigation
reporting_angles: Map the 14 reported encampment locations this week and interview affected residents and business owners about safety and sanitation concerns
Investigate why Bay Ridge—a relatively affluent waterfront neighborhood—is experiencing this spike now; interview DHS and local officials about resource allocation and shelter capacity

themes_detail.label: Outdoor Dining Complaints Explode
themes_detail.summary: Outdoor dining complaints surged to 5 this week—a 3900% spike from a 0.1 weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score: 14.74, highest severity)—suggesting rapid expansion of street or sidewalk dining that residents perceive as problematic this week.
evidence: 5 outdoor dining complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly baseline (3900% spike, z-score 14.74—highest statistical anomaly in dataset)
Zero outdoor dining complaints averaged over prior 8 weeks, making this a genuine emergence
Spike coincides with potential seasonal reopening or new restaurant/vendor activity
reporting_angles: Identify which restaurants or dining venues opened or expanded outdoor seating this week; interview neighbors about noise, blockage, or quality-of-life impacts
Cross-reference with mobile food vendor spike (4 complaints, +1500%) to determine if both outdoor dining and street vending are part of a single commercial expansion trend

themes_detail.label: Air Quality Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Air quality complaints jumped to 7 this week—a 700% increase from a 0.9 weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score: 5.82)—indicating a new pollution or odor issue affecting residents' perception of air quality this week.
evidence: 7 air quality complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.9 weekly baseline (700% spike, z-score 5.82)
Converges with standing water spike (4 complaints, +3100% this week), which could indicate water management or sewage issues producing odors
Converges with residential disposal complaint spike (10 last week, +196%), suggesting waste handling may be contributing to air quality concerns
reporting_angles: Interview complainants about the specific odor or pollutant and location; check whether reports cluster geographically around a single industrial site, landfill, or wastewater facility
Investigate if standing water + disposal complaints + air quality complaints form a connected sanitation infrastructure problem (e.g., backed-up sewers, waste staging area, storm drain failure)

themes_detail.label: Standing Water & Flooding Spike
themes_detail.summary: Standing water complaints hit 4 this week—a 3100% surge from a 0.1 weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score: 11.72)—suggesting a new drainage, flooding, or water retention problem across Bay Ridge/Dyker Heights this week.
evidence: 4 standing water complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly baseline (3100% spike, z-score 11.72)
Converges with air quality spike (7 this week, +700%), indicating stagnant water may be producing odors
Potential seasonal correlation with heavy rain or snowmelt; check weather data for this week
reporting_angles: Map the 4 standing water locations and determine if they reflect a single drainage failure (e.g., clogged storm drain, broken pipe) or distributed flooding across multiple streets
Interview DEP or DCP about recent storm event impacts and whether this represents a broader citywide infrastructure failure or a Bay Ridge-specific problem

themes_detail.label: Mobile Food Vendor Enforcement Tensions
themes_detail.summary: Mobile food vendor complaints spiked to 4 this week (+1500% from 0.2 weekly average, z-score 8.66), while vendor enforcement complaints reached 6 (+586% from 0.9 baseline, z-score 6.57), suggesting conflict between street vendors and residents or enforcement action this week.
evidence: 4 mobile food vendor complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly baseline (+1500%, z-score 8.66)
6 vendor enforcement complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.9 weekly baseline (+586%, z-score 6.57)
Paired spike suggests either new vendor activity OR enforcement crackdown triggering resident complaints about how enforcement is conducted
reporting_angles: Determine whether spike reflects new street vendors opening this week or increased police/DSNY enforcement; interview vendors and nearby residents about tensions
Cross-reference with outdoor dining spike (+3900%) to see if this is part of broader informal commerce expansion (vendors + outdoor dining proliferation in single week)
